entry.label: Conant-Ashby Theorem
entry.description: The Conant–Ashby theorem states, under the assumptions of the original formal paper, that the simplest optimal regulator must embody a model of what it regulates. Popular uses should not erase those assumptions or turn every useful representation into a proof of optimal control.
entry.canonical_definition: Under the paper's assumptions, a simplest optimal regulator is representable by a mapping h: S → R.

profile.title: Conant-Ashby Theorem
profile.summary: The result concerns the simplest regulator among those minimising outcome entropy. Its model is a mapping from reguland events to regulatory actions.
profile.canonical_definition: Under the paper's assumptions, a simplest optimal regulator is representable by a mapping h: S → R.
profile.why_it_matters: A diagram or forecast is not sufficient evidence that an organisation regulates successfully.
key_distinctions: an embodied mapping versus an explicit representation
a theorem's assumptions versus an organisational analogy
practice_connections: State which outcomes count as successful before invoking optimality.
common_misreadings: The model must be a conscious simulation.
open_checks: Assess how the theorem's fixed distribution and outcome criterion fit the proposed application.
